newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close sharply higher.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates ended sharply higher on Thursday as the central bank continued to mop up funds in the banking system despite generally tight liquidity, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate closed at 7.001 against Wednesday's 6.720 close -- far outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone -- with 30-day commercial paper rising to 7.00-7.25 percent against 6.75.

The central bank on Thursday issued T$3 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit, further squeezing the already tight liquidity in the banking system and prompting banks to adopt a conservative policy, dealers said.
Dealers said they did not rule out the possibility of further gains if the central bank continued to soak up liquidity on Friday.
The central bank has consistently denied that its repeated issuance of the short-term instruments in recent weeks intended to take some of the fire from the sizzling stock market.
Analysts are sceptical, saying persistently loose liquidity has been a key factor driving a huge stock rally that has pushed the share index 25 percent higher in 1997 alone.
The central bank appeared to tolerate the high short-term money rates to calm the stock fever, dealers said.
On Thursday, the stock index ended down 71.70 points or 0.83 percent at 8,584.12. Turnover was a sizzling T$197 billion.
The benchmark government bond yields rose in the earlier session, but no trade was reported in the afternoon.
Dealers expected a consolidation on Friday.
